title: Tanager SupplyChain — Pilot call synthesis and action hypotheses
body:
Context: quick synthesis of the 2026-02-27 kickoff call with Tanager SupplyChain (procurement + infra leads). This is my working scratch — not customer-facing. Purpose: capture constraints, product fit questions, and a prioritized set of technical next steps we can take before the next demo.

Attendees:
- Tanager: Priyanka Rao (Head of Platforms), Benji Mo (SRE), Alessa Tan (Data Privacy)
- Redwood: Maya Chen (SE), Owen Park (Solutions Eng), Lucia Alvarez (Security SME)

High-level ask from customer:
- Replace an internal rules-based assistant with an LLM endpoint for vendor communication summarization and anomaly detection in procurement flows. Needs on-prem deployment (air-gapped optional) and strict PII redaction + auditability. Target: 20k requests/day peak, median payload ~600 tokens, burst to 3k concurrent.

Immediate constraints & non-negotiables noted on call:
1) Data residency: all input/output logs must remain inside their VPC; they will not permit plaintext event storage in a managed plane.
2) KMS/HSM requirement for key wrapping of model keys and audit keys.
3) Network: egress strictly limited; only allow specific control-plane IPs for telemetry.
4) Compliance: need 90-day audit log retention + tamper-evident append-only logs (they asked for hash-chaining, need to follow up on spec).

SLO / Performance targets discussed:
- P95 latency for generation <= 420ms for median prompt (600 tokens) when under normal load (non-burst).
- Graceful degradation for bursts: fall back from base model -> distilled/q8 models with automatic quality monitoring and alerting.
- Cost target: aim for <= 0.8x current infra cost per token (they shared rough baseline of $0.012/token).

Preliminary integration architecture (working hypothesis):
- Private deployment inside customer VPC using Redwood Private (single control plane, local runtime).
- 2 node Dedicated-like pool (A100-equivalent) + autoscale to 6 nodes for burst; colocate with message queue (Kafka) for ingress buffering.
- Prefix/KV caching enabled with per-tenant cache TTL (configurable).
- KMS integration via customer HSM; we will support remote unwrap by Redwood control plane only if they approve a minimal egress allowlist.

Technical risks / gotchas identified (ranked):
1) Network egress policy vs. control plane callbacks — if they block our IP ranges, telemetry + automatic rollback may be disabled. Risk: higher ops overhead and slower incident response.
2) P95 latency target tight for 600-token workloads on 2 nodes unless batching and caching aggressively tuned. Need microbenchmarks with their prefix distribution.
3) Audit log format mismatch — their expected hash-chain scheme differs from our default audit schema; we must assess feasibility of exporting SHA-256 chained blobs to their S3/HSM.
4) Privacy/regulatory: redaction is model-dependent; relying solely on post-processing redaction is brittle. Consider a pre-filtering step + deterministic suppression for certain fields.
5) Model fallback quality regressions — need prompt-set based regression tests (they have 250 sample transcripts to share).

Notes & informal captures from the call (verbatim-ish):
- "No outside storage, ever — logs must live in our S3 behind our VPC endpoint" — Priyanka
- "We can carve a tiny public egress range for control plane, but it must be whitelisted and reviewed monthly." — Benji
- "If you can't do HSM-wrapped keys we can't proceed to PoC." — Alessa

Concrete next steps (with owners and rough ETA):
1) Maya: send minimal on-prem architecture diagram + list of control-plane IPs we need to communicate for telemetry & rollout (ETA: 2026-03-12).
2) Owen: run an internal microbenchmark simulating 600-token median prompts on quantized q8 models to validate P95 under a 2-node pool + 20k rps/day pattern (ETA: 2026-03-05). Output: P90/P95/P99 latency table + recommended node count.
3) Lucia: draft HSM keyflow options (local HSM vs Redwood-managed unwrap) and a gap analysis vs their security requirements (ETA: 2026-03-09).
4) Tanager -> share: sample 250 transcripts + current rules-based outputs, and their current token-cost baseline numbers (ETA: 2026-03-04).
5) Maya/Owen: prototype a redaction middleware (deterministic regex + model-assisted) and measure false positives/negatives on initial 50 transcripts (ETA: 2026-03-18).
6) All: sync on audit log hash-chaining format; create a small Confluence spec to iterate (Maya owner, ETA 2026-03-10).

Open questions to resolve (for next call):
- Can Tanager accept a small weekly telemetry heartbeat to our control plane rather than full request logs? What metadata is allowed?
- What are exact HSM vendors and APIs in their stack (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, etc.)? Need sample X.509s/endpoint docs.
- Do they expect model weights to be stored encrypted at rest only, or also attestable via remote attestation (SGX/TPM)?
- Clarify the acceptable latency envelope for fallback models — is 800ms P95 acceptable during bursts?

Quick risk mitigations proposed inline:
- If control-plane egress is blocked: propose a 'pull' mode where an ops-runbook Tarball is periodically pulled from their VPC by an approved admin VM and uploaded to secured bucket we can access — ugly but workable for PoC.
- For redaction: require two-phase redact (pre-filter + soft redact with confidence threshold) and surfacing of redaction candidates in the audit trail for manual review.

TODO checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] Send architecture diagram + IP list to Tanager (Maya)
- [ ] Benchmarks for q8 model latency (Owen)
- [ ] HSM integration options doc (Lucia)
- [ ] Receive transcripts and cost baseline (Tanager)
- [ ] Prototype redaction middleware (Maya/Owen)
- [ ] Draft audit log format spec and share (Maya)

Notes to self: prioritize benchmark before deep architecture changes. If q8 mode can't meet P95, discuss hybrid approach: small warm-hot higher-precision pool for median traffic + q8 cold pool for batch processing. Keep the first PoC minimal scope: summarization + anomaly detection, no live vendor-facing generations until redaction locks down.

Meeting cadence proposed: weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks; add security working session (Lucia + Alessa) for HSM & audit spec.

End / working copy.
